cfn_description: Hosted zone and record sets for podcastgarage.org
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Route53 hosted zone for the domain podcastgarage.org (with a trailing dot) and configures all necessary DNS record sets for the production environment, including TXT records for SPF (including mail.zendesk.com, _spf.createsend.com, _spf.google.com) and Google site verification with the token "google-site-verification=Yf4Jj6qY9hW7nIJzOxFX5Db_0rpezREwpeiWGWgbdDc", A records pointing to Squarespace IPs 198.185.159.144, 198.185.159.145, 198.49.23.144, and 198.49.23.145, a CNAME for www.podcastgarage.org to ext-cust.squarespace.com, MX records for G Suite with priorities 1,5,5,10,10 pointing to ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM, ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM, ALT2.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM, ASPMX2.GOOGLEMAIL.COM, and ASPMX3.GOOGLEMAIL.COM, a DMARC TXT record for _dmarc.podcastgarage.org with policy reject and reporting addresses dmarc-reports@prx.org and dmarc@qf66rrn4.uriports.com, an internal A record for colorprinter.podcastgarage.org pointing to 192.168.1.69, ZenDesk verification TXT record with value "c3d52cc061e9939d" and CNAME records for zendesk1 through zendesk4 pointing to mail1.zendesk.com through mail4.zendesk.com, plus DKIM CNAMEs for zendesk1._domainkey and zendesk2._domainkey pointing to the corresponding zendesk.com keys, a Google Workspace DKIM TXT record for google._domainkey with the provided RSA public key string, and Campaign Monitor DKIM TXT for cm._domainkey with its RSA public key, plus an SPF TXT for cm-bounce including _spf.createsend.com and MX records for cm-bounce pointing to mx20.inbound.createsend.com and mx21.inbound.createsend.com with priority 5. The hosted zone should be tagged with prx:meta:tagging-version "2021-04-07", prx:cloudformation:stack-name and stack-id referencing the stack, prx:ops:environment "Production", and prx:dev:application "Podcast Garage". The domain name should be configurable via a parameter defaulting to "podcastgarage.org." and all record sets must be associated with the hosted zone.
cfn_code:
# dns/podcastgarage.org-hosted_zone.yml
################################################################################
#### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! ########################################
#### THIS FILE IS CONTINUOUSLY DEPLOYED ########################################
#### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! ########################################
################################################################################
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Hosted zone and record sets for podcastgarage.org

Parameters:
  Domain:
    Default: podcastgarage.org.
    Description: The domain name and hosted zone
    Type: String

Resources:
  HostedZone:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HostedZone
    Properties:
      HostedZoneConfig:
        Comment: Podcast Garage domain
      HostedZoneTags:
        - { Key: prx:meta:tagging-version, Value: "2021-04-07" }
        - { Key: prx:cloudformation:stack-name, Value: !Ref AWS::StackName }
        - { Key: prx:cloudformation:stack-id, Value: !Ref AWS::StackId }
        - { Key: prx:ops:environment, Value: Production }
        - { Key: prx:dev:application, Value: Podcast Garage }
      Name: !Ref Domain

  # Purpose-based
  Text:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      # Route53 expects TXT record values to be enclosed in double quotes, so in
      # the YAML they need to be double-quoted.
      # Each domain name should only have a single text record. Add multiple
      # resource records if necessary.
      # All SPF records need to go into a single resource record.
      Comment: TXT Records
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      RecordSets:
        - Name: !Ref Domain
          ResourceRecords:
            # SPF
            - '"v=spf1 include:mail.zendesk.com include:_spf.createsend.com include:_spf.google.com -all"'
            # Domain verification
            - '"google-site-verification=Yf4Jj6qY9hW7nIJzOxFX5Db_0rpezREwpeiWGWgbdDc"'
          TTL: "300"
          Type: TXT
  Web:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      Comment: Website on Squarespace
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      RecordSets:
        - Name: !Ref Domain
          ResourceRecords:
            - 198.185.159.144
            - 198.185.159.145
            - 198.49.23.144
            - 198.49.23.145
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: A
        - Name: !Sub www.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - ext-cust.squarespace.com.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: CNAME
  Email:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      Comment: G Suite
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      RecordSets:
        # Mail exchange
        - Name: !Ref Domain
          ResourceRecords:
            - 1 ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.
            - 5 ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.
            - 5 ALT2.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.
            - 10 ASPMX2.GOOGLEMAIL.COM.
            - 10 ASPMX3.GOOGLEMAIL.COM.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: MX
        # DMARC
        - Name: !Sub _dmarc.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - '"v=DMARC1; p=reject; pct=100; ri=86400; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@prx.org,mailto:dmarc@qf66rrn4.uriports.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc-reports@prx.org,mailto:dmarc@qf66rrn4.uriports.com; aspf=r; adkim=r"'
          TTL: "300"
          Type: TXT
  Internal:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      Comment: Internal
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      RecordSets:
        - Name: !Sub colorprinter.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - 192.168.1.69
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: A

  # Service-specific
  ZenDesk:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      Comment: ZenDesk
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      RecordSets:
        - Name: !Sub zendesk_verification.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - '"c3d52cc061e9939d"'
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: TXT
        # Domain Validation
        - Name: !Sub zendesk1.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail1.zendesk.com.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: CNAME
        - Name: !Sub zendesk2.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail2.zendesk.com.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: CNAME
        - Name: !Sub zendesk3.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail3.zendesk.com.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: CNAME
        - Name: !Sub zendesk4.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail4.zendesk.com.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: CNAME
        # DKIM
        - Name: !Sub zendesk1._domainkey.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - zendesk1._domainkey.zendesk.com.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: CNAME
        - Name: !Sub zendesk2._domainkey.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - zendesk2._domainkey.zendesk.com.
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: CNAME
  GoogleWorkspace:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      Comment: Google Workspace
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      RecordSets:
        # DKIM
        # This is the public key matching a private key that Google Workspace
        # uses to sign emails it send on our behalf
        # https://admin.google.com/ac/apps/gmail/authenticateemail
        - Name: !Sub google._domainkey.${Domain}
          ResourceRecords:
            - '"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAw+AmkgYZZPfQKXQGd3XDY7a8BG4Z0ytBzcjwB3JmUEcQzKO8bBB/3n+Vr9d4xjcn8ISIxbvxHaF0CG93AOKM0KVy6qgog/E7eStuwp4aVbjY+x2Nr1cD/0TizRXnn78U3zFoM72Eb491zpDHYYHPOlu2zFIlb3OmYwqf1Qp67QcnZkf9rkMqCwD6/4tiG+Gpi" "VPgY2eMkhM5GGBE1en9ytBqeJYdLtfv4YqMG8bb68x+HwWJ1WdJSH3pPqjtmy/7kSFrrSxYFx4ReIPeLHKztrA8n2MNs1LG1yzTDgxvG7819DRF6BS18uQZrbC5wNoypkEJ7C5vX7Bu1Ns/K0AaDwIDAQAB"'
          TTL: "3600"
          Type: TXT
  CampaignMonitor:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      Comment: Campaign Monitor
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      RecordSets:
        # DKIM

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS task definition for a containerized application, along with the necessary IAM roles and logging infrastructure to support it. The template should include a parameter for the ECR repository name with a default value of "book-app", which will be used as the family name for the task definition and as a prefix for the log stream. We need two IAM roles: a task role that allows the ECS task to interact with AWS Systems Manager Session Manager messaging channels (specifically the ssmmessages actions for creating and opening control and data channels) to enable ECS Exec functionality, and a task execution role that uses the managed AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy to allow ECS to pull container images and write logs to CloudWatch. Both roles should be assumable by the ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com service principal and should have names prefixed with the CloudFormation stack name followed by "-TaskRole" and "-TaskExecutionRole" respectively. The task definition itself should use the Fargate launch type with the awsvpc network mode, allocate 256 CPU units and 512 MB of memory, and define a single container using the public nginx image from public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx, mapping container port 80, with the container not running in privileged mode. The container should have logging configured to send logs to a CloudWatch log group using the awslogs driver, with the log group named "/ecs/book-app" (or more precisely, "/ecs/" followed by the ECR repository name parameter value), set to retain logs for 7 days, and the log stream prefix should match the ECR repository name. The log group should be deleted when the stack is deleted. The template should export the task definition ARN, task role ARN, and task execution role ARN as outputs with names suffixed by "-task-def", "-task-role", and "-task-execution-role" respectively, all prefixed with the stack name, so that other stacks can reference these resources.
cfn_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: ECS Task Definition
#------------------------------------------------------
# Parameters
#------------------------------------------------------
Parameters:
  EcrRepoName:
    Type: String
    Description: Name of the ecr repo
    Default: book-app
#------------------------------------------------------
# Resources: task role, task execution role
#------------------------------------------------------
Resources:
  TaskRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Metadata:
      cfn_nag:
        rules_to_suppress:
          - id: W11
            reason: "enable exec into task"
          - id: W28
            reason: "use expicit post-fix task role name for demo"
    Properties:
      RoleName:
        !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-TaskRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Action:
              - "sts:AssumeRole"
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: root
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - "ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel"
                  - "ssmmessages:CreateDataChannel"
                  - "ssmmessages:OpenControlChannel"
                  - "ssmmessages:OpenDataChannel"
                Resource: "*"

  TaskExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Metadata:
      cfn_nag:
        rules_to_suppress:
          - id: W28
            reason: "use expicit post-fix task role name for demo"
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-TaskExecutionRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Action:
              - "sts:AssumeRole"
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy

  #------------------------------------------------------
  # Task Definition
  #------------------------------------------------------
  TaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Ref EcrRepoName
      TaskRoleArn: !GetAtt TaskRole.Arn
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt TaskExecutionRole.Arn
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      Cpu: 256
      Memory: 512
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: !Ref EcrRepoName
          Image: public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: 80
          Privileged: false
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: awslogs
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Ref LogGroup
              awslogs-region: !Ref AWS::Region
              awslogs-stream-prefix: !Ref EcrRepoName
  LogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Metadata:
      cfn_nag:
        rules_to_suppress:
          - id: W84
            reason: "skip using KMS for demo purpose"
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      LogGroupName:
        !Sub
          - "/ecs/${EcrRepoName}"
          - EcrRepoName: !Ref EcrRepoName
      RetentionInDays: 7

#------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
#------------------------------------------------------
Outputs:
  TaskDefinition:
    Description: Task Definition
    Value: !Ref TaskDefinition
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-task-def"
  TaskRole:
    Description: Task Role
    Value: !Ref TaskRole
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-task-role"
  TaskExecutionRole:
    Description: Task Execution Role
    Value: !Ref TaskExecutionRole
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-task-execution-role"

cfn_description: FisWorkshopAccessControls
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates four IAM roles for fine-grained access control to AWS Fault Injection Simulator (FIS) experiments, intended to support a workshop scenario where different personas have varying levels of permissions while enforcing a security boundary that denies any FIS actions on resources tagged with Environment=prod. The template must define roles named FisAccessControlSecurityAdmin, FisAccessControlAdmin, FisAccessControlUser, and FisAccessControlNonUser, each with a trust policy that allows the same account’s principal to sts:AssumeRole. All four roles must have the AWS managed ReadOnlyAccess policy attached. The FisAccessControlSecurityAdmin role should have an inline policy granting full fis:* access, the ability to pass the FisWorkshopServiceRole and FisWorkshopSpotRole execution roles to the FIS service (via iam:PassRole with a condition on iam:PassedToService equal to fis.amazonaws.com), and permission to create service-linked roles. The FisAccessControlAdmin role should allow full fis:* except for a Deny statement that blocks any fis:* action on resources where the Environment tag equals prod, and also include the same PassRole and service-linked role creation permissions. The FisAccessControlUser role should permit fis:Get*, fis:List*, fis:StartExperiment, and fis:StopExperiment, along with fis:TagResource limited to experiments in the us-west-2 region (arn:aws:fis:us-west-2::experiment/*), a Deny on prod-tagged resources, and the same PassRole and service-linked role creation capabilities. The FisAccessControlNonUser role must explicitly deny all fis:* actions while still allowing service-linked role creation. The PassRole resources must be the exact ARNs for FisWorkshopServiceRole and FisWorkshopSpotRole, and all roles should include a statement to allow iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole on any resource.

Description: FisWorkshopAccessControls

        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess

        - PolicyName: AllowFisFullAccess

            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowAllFis

                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: AllowServiceLinkedRoleCreation
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: DenyFisProdAccess
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    "aws:ResourceTag/Environment": "prod"

                Action:
                  - fis:*
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: AllowPassingExecutionRole
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    "iam:PassedToService": "fis.amazonaws.com"
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:PassRole
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/FisWorkshopServiceRole'
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/FisWorkshopSpotRole'

        Version: "2012-10-17"

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with a CIDR block of 172.31.0.0/16, along with two public subnets (172.31.1.0/24 in us-east-1a and 172.31.3.0/24 in us-east-1b) and two private subnets (172.31.2.0/24 in us-east-1a and 172.31.4.0/24 in us-east-1b), where public subnets have auto-assign public IP enabled and private subnets do not; the template should also provision an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC, a NAT Gateway placed in the first public subnet with an associated Elastic IP (domain vpc), separate public and private route tables for each subnet with default routes (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to the Internet Gateway for public subnets and to the NAT Gateway for private subnets, and proper subnet-to-route-table associations; all resources must be tagged with a key "ResourceType" set to "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3" and appropriate Name tags; finally, the stack should export the VPC ID and the IDs of all four subnets using the stack name as a prefix, and also output the stack name itself.
cfn_code:
Resources:
  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create a VPC with a public and private subnet across two AZs
  #------------------------------------------------------------
  Pattern3VPC:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::VPC'
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 172.31.0.0/16
      Tags:
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicSubnet1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1a
      CidrBlock: 172.31.1.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: true
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicSubnet1"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicSubnet2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1b
      CidrBlock: 172.31.3.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: true
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicSubnet2"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1a
      CidrBlock: 172.31.2.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateSubnet1"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Subnet'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      AvailabilityZone: us-east-1b
      CidrBlock: 172.31.4.0/24
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateSubnet2"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  #-------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create an IGW and attach to the created VPC
  # Create a NAT GW with an associated public IP address.
  #-------------------------------------------------------------

  Pattern3IGW:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "igw"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3IGWAttach:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref Pattern3IGW

  Pattern3NatGateway:
    Type: "AWS::EC2::NatGateway"
    DependsOn: Pattern3NatPublicIP
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt Pattern3NatPublicIP.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet1
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "nat"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3NatPublicIP:
    Type: "AWS::EC2::EIP"
    DependsOn: Pattern3VPC
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
      Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "NatPublicIP"]]
      - Key: ResourceType
        Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  #-------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create public route table and attach to the public subnets
  #-------------------------------------------------------------

  Pattern3PublicRouteTable1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicRouteTable1"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicRouteTable2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PublicRouteTable2"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PublicRoute1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn:
      - Pattern3IGW
      - Pattern3IGWAttach
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable1
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref Pattern3IGW

  Pattern3PublicRoute2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn:
      - Pattern3IGW
      - Pattern3IGWAttach
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable2
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref Pattern3IGW

  Pattern3PublicSubnet1RouteTableAssociation1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet1
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable1

  Pattern3PublicSubnet1RouteTableAssociation2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PublicSubnet2
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PublicRouteTable2

  #-------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create public route table and attach to the public subnets
  #-------------------------------------------------------------

  Pattern3PrivateRouteTable1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateRouteTable1"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateRouteTable2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::RouteTable'
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Pattern3VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Join ["-", [!Ref Pattern3VPC, "PrivateRouteTable2"]]
        - Key: ResourceType
          Value: "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3"

  Pattern3PrivateRoute1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn: Pattern3IGW
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable1
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref Pattern3NatGateway

  Pattern3PrivateRoute2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::Route'
    DependsOn: Pattern3IGW
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable2
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref Pattern3NatGateway

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet1RouteTableAssociation1:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateSubnet1
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable1

  Pattern3PrivateSubnet1RouteTableAssociation2:
    Type: 'AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation'
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateSubnet2
      RouteTableId: !Ref Pattern3PrivateRouteTable2

# Output section

Outputs:

    Description: Stack name
    Value: !Ref AWS::StackName
  OutputPattern3VPC:
    Description: Baseline VPC
    Value: !Ref Pattern3VPC
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-VpcId"
  OutputPattern3PublicSubnet1:

    Export:

  OutputPattern3PublicSubnet2:

cfn_code:
---
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Publishes two builder Lambdas (x86_64 and arm64) that back a CFN Custom
  Resource. Consumers import the ServiceToken matching the architecture of the
  layer they want built: cfn:lambdalayer-x86-64:<region>:arn or
  cfn:lambdalayer-arm64:<region>:arn.
Metadata:
  Author: KissT
  Project: CFN-CR-PythonLambdaLayer
  SourceCode: https://github.com/kisst/CFN-CR-PythonLambdaLayer

Parameters:
  LogLevel:
    Type: String
    Description: Python logging level for the builder Lambdas. Update the stack to flip verbosity without code changes.
    Default: INFO
    AllowedValues: [CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO, DEBUG, NOTSET]

Resources:
  LambdaLambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: 'AWS::IAM::Role'
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Path: /
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AllowLogs
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: 2012-10-17
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/cfn-cr-python-lambda-layer-x86_64'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/cfn-cr-python-lambda-layer-x86_64:*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/cfn-cr-python-lambda-layer-arm64'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/cfn-cr-python-lambda-layer-arm64:*'
        - PolicyName: AllowLambda
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: 2012-10-17
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lambda:PublishLayerVersion
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:lambda:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:layer:*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lambda:GetLayerVersion
                  - lambda:GetLayerVersionPolicy
                  - lambda:ListLayerVersions
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:lambda:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:layer:*:*'

  LayerBuilderX8664Function:
    Type: 'AWS::Lambda::Function'
    Properties:
      FunctionName: cfn-cr-python-lambda-layer-x86_64
      Description: 'Build a lambda layer with given requirements (x86_64)'
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import base64
          import contextlib
          import logging
          import os
          import platform
          import subprocess
          import sys
          import zipfile
          import boto3
          try:
              import cfnresponse
              CFN_CALL = True
          except ImportError:
              CFN_CALL = False

          BUILDER_RUNTIME = f"python{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}"
          _ARCH_MAP = {"x86_64": "x86_64", "aarch64": "arm64"}
          BUILDER_ARCHITECTURE = _ARCH_MAP.get(platform.machine(), platform.machine())

          PKG_ROOT = "/tmp/packages"
          PKG_DIR = f"{PKG_ROOT}/python/lib/{BUILDER_RUNTIME}/site-packages"

          _LEVEL_NAME = os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO").upper()
          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.getLevelNamesMapping().get(_LEVEL_NAME, logging.INFO))

          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              try:
                  request_type = event['RequestType']
                  resource_properties = event['ResourceProperties']

                  name = resource_properties['Name']
                  region = context.invoked_function_arn.split(':')[3]

                  if request_type not in ('Create', 'Update'):
                      exit_gracefully("Nothing to do here", event, context)

                  job_to_do = False
                  try:
                      install_with_pip(resource_properties['requirements'])
                      job_to_do = True
                  except KeyError:
                      pass

                  try:
                      dump_text_to_file(
                          resource_properties['filename'],
                          resource_properties['filecontent'],
                          PKG_DIR
                      )
                      job_to_do = True
                  except KeyError:
                      pass

                  if job_to_do:
                      zipit(PKG_ROOT, "/tmp/layer")
                      compatible_runtimes = resource_properties.get(
                          'CompatibleRuntimes', [BUILDER_RUNTIME]
                      )
                      compatible_architectures = resource_properties.get(
                          'CompatibleArchitectures', [BUILDER_ARCHITECTURE]
                      )
                      layer_arn = publish_layer(
                          name, region, compatible_runtimes, compatible_architectures
                      )
                      if CFN_CALL:
                          data = {"Arn": layer_arn}
                          cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.SUCCESS, data, layer_arn)
                  else:

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ElastiCache Redis cluster along with its associated security group and a Route53 CNAME record, designed for a UAT environment. The template should reference an existing VPC and Route53 private hosted zone through cross-stack imports, using the default stack names "UAT-VPC" and "UAT-Route53" respectively. The nested stack templates should be pulled from an S3 bucket named "dchash2buildbucket" in the ap-southeast-2 region, with the security group template file named "EC2-SecurityGroup-ElastiCacheRedis.yaml", the Redis cluster template file named "ElastiCache-Redis.yaml", and the Route53 record set template file named "Route53-RecordSet.yaml". The Redis cluster should be configurable with a cache node type defaulting to cache.t2.micro, allowing selection from t2 and m4 instance families, a number of cache clusters between 1 and 3 defaulting to 1, a port defaulting to 6379, and a maintenance window defaulting to "Sun:05:00-Sun:07:00". The template must support high availability by enabling auto-failover when more than one cache cluster is specified, and the cluster should be placed in the private subnets imported from the VPC stack (PrivateSubnetA, PrivateSubnetB, PrivateSubnetC). The security group should be created within the imported VPC and passed to the Redis cluster. The Route53 record should be a CNAME type with a TTL of 300 seconds, using the hostname "DCHash2redis" and the private domain name imported from the Route53 stack, pointing to the Redis cluster's connection endpoint. All resources must be tagged with environment (defaulting to UAT, with options for Production or Test), business unit (defaulting to Gaming, with options for Charitable, Corporate, Lotteries, or Wagering), department (defaulting to BrandName), application (defaulting to SomePlatform), and component (defaulting to ElastiCache-Redis). The template should export the cache connection address and security group ID as stack outputs for use by other stacks.

        VPCID:
          Fn::ImportValue: !Sub ${VPCStackName}-VPCID
        SubnetList:
          Fn::Join:
          - ","
          - - Fn::ImportValue: !Sub ${VPCStackName}-PrivateSubnetA
            - Fn::ImportValue: !Sub ${VPCStackName}-PrivateSubnetB
            - Fn::ImportValue: !Sub ${VPCStackName}-PrivateSubnetC
        SecurityGroup: !GetAtt [ SecurityGroup, Outputs.SecurityGroup ]

  # Add Redis endpoint to Route53
  Route53RecordSet:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
    Properties:
      TemplateURL: !Sub https://s3-ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/${BuildBucket}/${Route53RecordSetTemplateFile}
      Parameters:
        AliasTarget: ''
        AliasHostedZoneId: ''
        HostedZoneName: ''
        RecordType: CNAME
        HostName: !Ref HostName
        DomainName:
          Fn::ImportValue: !Sub ${DomainStackName}-Private-DomainName
        TTL: 300
        DestinationAddress: !GetAtt [ ElastiCacheRedisCluster, Outputs.CacheConnection ]

Outputs:
  CacheConnection:
    Description: ElastiCache Connection address
    Value: !GetAtt [ElastiCacheRedisCluster, Outputs.CacheConnection]
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-CacheConnection"

  SecurityGroup:
    Description: The App1-php Security Group
    Value:  !GetAtt [ SecurityGroup, Outputs.SecurityGroup ]
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-SecurityGroup"

cfn_description: Deploy a service into an ECS cluster behind a private load balancer.
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS service running an nginx container behind a private Application Load Balancer, designed to be deployed as part of a larger parent cluster stack named "production" which provides the cluster name, VPC ID, and private listener ARN via cross-stack exports. The template should accept parameters for the service name (defaulting to nginx), the Docker image URL (defaulting to nginx), the container port (defaulting to 80), CPU units (defaulting to 256), memory in megabytes (defaulting to 512), a path pattern for routing traffic (defaulting to "*" to catch all paths), a priority for the listener rule (defaulting to 1), the desired number of running tasks (defaulting to 2), and an optional IAM role ARN for the task if the container needs access to other AWS resources. The template must conditionally assign the task role only when a custom role is provided. It should create an ECS task definition with the specified CPU, memory, and container port mapping, an ECS service that runs the desired count of tasks with a deployment configuration allowing up to 200% during deployments and maintaining at least 75% healthy instances, an Application Load Balancer target group on port 80 with HTTP health checks every 6 seconds, a 5-second timeout, 2 healthy and 2 unhealthy thresholds, and a listener rule on the imported private listener that forwards traffic matching the specified path pattern to the target group with the given priority. The service must depend on the listener rule to ensure proper ordering. All resources should use the service name as the family name for the task definition and the target group name.
cfn_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Deploy a service into an ECS cluster behind a private load balancer.
Parameters:
  StackName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: The name of the parent cluster stack that you created. Necessary
                 to locate and reference resources created by that stack.
  ServiceName:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: A name for the service
  ImageUrl:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: The url of a docker image that contains the application process that
                 will handle the traffic for this service
  ContainerPort:
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
    Description: What port number the application inside the docker container is binding to
  ContainerCpu:
    Type: Number
    Default: 256
    Description: How much CPU to give the container. 1024 is 1 CPU
  ContainerMemory:
    Type: Number
    Default: 512
    Description: How much memory in megabytes to give the container
  Path:
    Type: String
    Default: "*"
    Description: A path on the public load balancer that this service
                 should be connected to. Use * to send all load balancer
                 traffic to this service.
  Priority:
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
    Description: The priority for the routing rule added to the load balancer.
                 This only applies if your have multiple services which have been
                 assigned to different paths on the load balancer.
  DesiredCount:
    Type: Number
    Default: 2
    Description: How many copies of the service task to run
  Role:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: (Optional) An IAM role to give the service's containers if the code within needs to
                 access other AWS resources like S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, etc

Conditions:
  HasCustomRole: !Not [ !Equals [!Ref 'Role', ''] ]

Resources:

  # The task definition. This is a simple metadata description of what
  # container to run, and what resource requirements it has.
  TaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
      Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
      TaskRoleArn:
        Fn::If:
          - 'HasCustomRole'
          - !Ref 'Role'
          - !Ref "AWS::NoValue"
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
          Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
          Image: !Ref 'ImageUrl'
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'

  # The service. The service is a resource which allows you to run multiple
  # copies of a type of task, and gather up their logs and metrics, as well
  # as monitor the number of running tasks and replace any that have crashed
  Service:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    DependsOn: LoadBalancerRule
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cluster:
        Fn::ImportValue:
          !Join [':', [!Ref 'StackName', 'ClusterName']]
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MaximumPercent: 200
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 75
      DesiredCount: !Ref 'DesiredCount'
      TaskDefinition: !Ref 'TaskDefinition'
      LoadBalancers:
        - ContainerName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'

  # A target group. This is used for keeping track of all the tasks, and
  # what IP addresses / port numbers they have. You can query it yourself,
  # to use the addresses yourself, but most often this target group is just
  # connected to an application load balancer, or network load balancer, so
  # it can automatically distribute traffic across all the targets.
  TargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 6
      HealthCheckPath: /
      HealthCheckProtocol: HTTP
      HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
      HealthyThresholdCount: 2
      Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      UnhealthyThresholdCount: 2
      VpcId:
        Fn::ImportValue:
          !Join [':', [!Ref 'StackName', 'VPCId']]

  # Create a rule on the load balancer for routing traffic to the target group
  LoadBalancerRule:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule
    Properties:
      Actions:
        - TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'
          Type: 'forward'
      Conditions:
        - Field: path-pattern
          Values: [!Ref 'Path']
      ListenerArn:
        Fn::ImportValue:
          !Join [':', [!Ref 'StackName', 'PrivateListener']]
      Priority: !Ref 'Priority'
